fixed.item: breakages (pets, P1 gate G7): the pets share of the substep-cost regression (gate record: pets systems 0.190 ms per substep vs ADOPT 0.141; pets.agents 0.135 vs 0.106)
fixed.how: Measured first: the steady state equals ADOPT's (0.107 vs 0.105 ms per substep on one machine); the whole increase is the first substep of each house, where the kernel's static indexes (review M3: read view per entity inside a busy step) built pets' per-substep indexes (about 3.2 ms per house, 0.085 ms per substep of the bench). Fix (house_sim/systems/pets/common.py and the predicate sites in behavior, water, cages, aquatic, feeding, perception, physical, handling, yard): every pets index predicate is a named function declaring every field it reads (common.index_reads -> World.static_index reads=); the 15 indexes the time systems and idle probes look up every substep are registered (common.per_substep_index / PREBUILT) and built by common.prebuild_indexes at episode_start order -80, before any hook writes, so the World evaluates them on the plain records; the agents' water and litter-box sets now share the water systems' and litter system's indexes (same predicates: three copies of the water-holder index and two of the litter-box index were built before); common.pet_rooms gathers each room's connections in one pass instead of a sorted scan of every connection per room visited (the steady state's largest pets cost). No result changes: the content of an index is a pure function of the state (World.static_index), pet_rooms returns the same set.
